programs.title_tr: Pratt & Whitney GTF (PW1100G) Toz Metal Kusuru & Yere İndirmeler
programs.title_en: Pratt & Whitney GTF (PW1100G) Powder Metal Defect & Groundings
programs.current_status_tr: Yüksek basınçlı türbin disklerindeki mikroskobik toz metal kirliliği nedeniyle küresel çapta yüzlerce A320neo/A321neo uçağı planlanmamış motor bakımına alındı. Ortalama motor revizyon süresi (TAT) 250-300 günü buluyor.
programs.current_status_en: Contaminated powder metal in high-pressure turbine disks required accelerated inspections; hundreds of A320neo family jets grounded globally with MRO shop turnaround times reaching 250-300 days.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: THY filosundaki yaklaşık 30-40 adet A320/A321neo uçağı yerde bekliyor; kapasite açığını kapatmak için ıslak kiralama (wet lease) ve mevcut A320ceo uçaklarının hizmet ömrünü uzatma yoluna gidildi. Pegasus filosu ağırlıklı CFM LEAP motorlu olduğu için doğrudan etkilenmedi.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Turkish Airlines has 30-40 A321neo aircraft parked; capacity shortfall managed via wet leases and extending older A320ceo service lives. Pegasus remains largely unaffected due to CFM LEAP engine selection.
programs.timeline_horizon: 2026 yılı boyunca ve 2027 ilk yarısına kadar sürmesi bekleniyor.
programs.source_reference: RTX Corporation / FAA Airworthiness Directives (AD 2024-0044) / THY KAP Açıklamaları

programs.title_tr: Boeing 737 MAX Üretim Kısıtı (FAA Aylık 38 Tavanı) & Tedarik Zinciri
programs.title_en: Boeing 737 MAX FAA Monthly 38 Cap & Supply Chain Bottlecks
programs.current_status_tr: FAA'in kalite ve montaj denetimleri kapsamında Boeing 737 üretimini aylık 38 uçak tavanında tutması ve Spirit AeroSystems gövde teslimat gecikmeleri nedeniyle 2026 teslimat takvimleri 3-6 ay geriye ötelendi. MAX 7 ve MAX 10 sertifikasyonu gecikmeye devam ediyor.
programs.current_status_en: FAA capped 737 production at 38/month pending quality audit milestones; Spirit AeroSystems fuselage supply constraints pushed airline delivery slots back by 3 to 6 months. MAX 7 and MAX 10 certification remains pending.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: SunExpress ve THY teslimatları planlanan takvimin gerisinde seyrediyor; havayolları yoğun yaz ve sonbahar kapasite planlamalarını mevcut gövdelerle optimize ediyor.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: SunExpress and Turkish Airlines delivery streams experiencing slot postponements; carriers optimizing utilization on existing fleet assets.
programs.timeline_horizon: Aylık 38 üretim tavanının 2026 sonuna kadar aşamalı olarak artırılması hedefleniyor.
programs.source_reference: FAA Oversight Directives / Boeing Quarterly Deliveries / Airline Fleet Filings

programs.title_tr: Airbus A321XLR Ticari Teslimatları & Dar Gövde Uzun Menzil Devrimi
programs.title_en: Airbus A321XLR Entry into Service & Long-Range Narrowbody Wave
programs.current_status_tr: EASA tip sertifikasyonunu tamamlayan A321XLR, Iberia tarafından Madrid-Boston hattında ilk ticari uçuşlarına başladı. 4.700 deniz mili (8.700 km) menziliyle dar gövdede transatlantik ve kıtalararası uçuş maliyetlerini %30 düşürüyor.
programs.current_status_en: Having achieved EASA certification, the A321XLR commenced transatlantic operations with launch customer Iberia. Its 4,700 nm range unlocks thin long-haul routes at 30% lower trip cost.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: Orta Doğu, Afrika ve ikincil Avrupa şehirlerine doğrudan bağlantı potansiyeli nedeniyle bölge taşıyıcıları tarafından yakından izleniyor. THY ve Pegasus filo stratejilerinde uzun vadeli alternatif.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Closely monitored by regional carriers for secondary point-to-point routes into Africa, Central Asia and Europe; potential long-term fit for Istanbul network.
programs.source_reference: EASA Type Certificate Data Sheet (TCDS) / Airbus Commercial Aircraft Updates

programs.title_tr: Boeing 777-9 (777X) Test Uçuşları & Hizmete Giriş Tarihi
programs.current_status_tr: İtiş kolu bağlantı elemanındaki (thrust link) teknik arıza sonrası test uçuşları geçici olarak durdurulmuştu; Boeing ilk teslimat takvimini 2026 yılına (ve potansiyel olarak 2027'ye) revize etti. Başta Emirates ve Lufthansa olmak üzere amiral gemisi filoları A380 ve 777-300ER ömür uzatmak zorunda kaldı.
programs.current_status_en: Structural component inspection on engine thrust links required test fleet pause; initial deliveries rescheduled to 2026/2027. Major customers Emirates and Lufthansa forced to extend legacy 777-300ER and A380 service lives.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: THY'nin geniş gövde siparişlerinde Airbus A350-1000'e ağırlık vermesinde 777X gecikmeleri belirleyici stratejik etken oldu.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Delays were a primary catalyst for Turkish Airlines' decision to anchor its high-capacity widebody order book on the Airbus A350-1000.
programs.timeline_horizon: FAA tip sertifikasyonu ve ilk ticari teslimat 2026 sonu / 2027 hedefleniyor.
programs.source_reference: Boeing Defense, Space & Security / Airline IR Filings / Emirates President Statements

programs.title_tr: CFM LEAP-1A / 1B Yüksek Basınç Türbini Dayanıklılığı & MRO Bekleme Süreleri
programs.title_en: CFM LEAP-1A / 1B Hot-Section Durability & Shop Visit Backlogs
programs.current_status_tr: Sıcak iklim, tozlu hava sahası ve yüksek iniş-kalkış döngüsü altında çalışan LEAP motorlarında türbin kanatçığı erozyonu nedeniyle planlanandan erken motor indirme yaşanıyor. Küresel MRO atölyelerinde yedek parça ve motor kıtlığı devam ediyor.
programs.current_status_en: Harsh environment operations (heat, sand, high cycle utilization) causing premature hot-section turbine blade wear; global MRO shops experiencing parts constraints and extended turn-around times.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: Pegasus'un filosunun belkemiğini oluşturan A321neo uçaklarında CFM LEAP-1A motorları kullanılıyor. Pegasus, proaktif motor rotasyonu ve yedek motor rezervasyonu ile uçak yerde kalma süresini (AOG) asgaride tutuyor.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Pegasus relies heavily on CFM LEAP-1A on its A321neo fleet; carrier leverages proactive engine rotation and buffer lease pools to keep AOG rates minimal.
programs.timeline_horizon: CFM'in güncellenmiş dayanıklı parça (durability kit) teslimatları 2026 boyunca yaygınlaşıyor.
programs.source_reference: Safran / GE Aerospace Engine Technical Briefings / Aviation Week MRO Watch

stories.headline: United Airlines Focuses on Premium Experience and Loyalty to Drive Retention
stories.lead: An 18-page report by IdeaWorksCompany highlights United Airlines' strategy centered on premium customer proposition, loyalty programs, co-branded credit cards, and ancillary revenue. Authored by Jay Sorensen, the report examines initiatives introduced throughout 2025 and 2026.
stories.source_description: United Airlines is rapidly reshaping its customer proposition around premium experiences, loyalty, co-branded cards and ancillary revenue, according to a new 18-page IdeaWorksCompany report, “United is Winning the Race for Brand-Loyal Consumers.” Written by airline revenue and loyalty expert Jay Sorensen, the report examines United’s expanding portfolio of products and strategies introduced during 2025 and 2026. United’s lounge network, with 50+ locations, is another critical component of its brand-loyal strategy. The report estimates its network serves about 70,000 daily guests. That’s more than 25 million guests per year, which is equal to the annual passenger traffic of JetBlue. The report also examines United’s “Base” fares for the Premium Plus and Polaris cabins, which removes certain benefits, such as Polaris lounge access and advance seat assignments, for a lower fare.
detailed_analysis: United's lounge network comprises 50+ locations and is estimated to serve about 70,000 daily guests.
The carrier's annual lounge traffic exceeds 25 million guests per year, matching the total annual passenger traffic of JetBlue.
The report examines United's introduction of Base fares within its Premium Plus and Polaris cabins.
Strategic focus centers on expanding co-branded credit card integration, loyalty engagement, and premium service offerings.
stories.strategic_impact: Investing in premium lounges and cabin unbundling enables legacy carriers to capture higher yields, drive loyalty engagement, and grow co-branded credit card revenues.

stories.headline: Aeroitalia Selects Delta TechOps for 737 Fleet Component Support
stories.lead: Aeroitalia has contracted Delta TechOps to deliver comprehensive component maintenance support and material resources for its Boeing 737 fleet. The agreement was announced at MRO Europe in Amsterdam on Oct. 28 as the Italian carrier continues its regional expansion.
stories.source_description: Aeroitalia has selected Delta TechOps to provide comprehensive component support for its Boeing 737 fleet, reflecting growing demand for TechOps' commercial maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) capabilities among European carriers. Announced at MRO Europe in Amsterdam on Oct. 28, the program gives Aeroitalia access to Delta TechOps' component maintenance expertise and materials resources, helping maximize fleet reliability and aircraft availability as the carrier continues to grow. Supporting Italy’s newest airline "At Delta, we know firsthand what it takes to run a reliable airline every day,” said Marc Meredith, Chief Commercial Officer for Delta TechOps. “As Aeroitalia continues to grow across Italy and Europe, we're proud to have been selected to support its 737 fleet with the same operational expertise and unwavering focus on safety and performance that power Delta's own operation.” The announcement builds on an existing relationship between Delta and Aeroitalia. In 2025, Aeroitalia announced new connectivity opportunities between its domestic Italian network and Delta's global network. This latest step extends the relationship into maintenance and technical operations between the two airlines. “Celebrating this partnership at MRO Europe in Amsterdam marks an important milestone for Aeroitalia. Our agreement with Delta TechOps, a leading MRO provider of MRO services, will enable us to improve the operational efficiency of our Boeing 737 NG fleet. By combining a component-sharing system with a dedicated spare parts kit at our main base, we will be able to reduce procurement times for replacement parts, minimize aircraft downtime and increase fleet availability. This will help reduce operational disruptions and it will allow us to offer a more reliable service to our passengers,” said Fabrizio Liberatori, Group Accountable Manager at Aeroitalia. Building a Global MRO Business The Aeroitalia award is the latest addition to Delta TechOps' MRO expanding components portfolio. Following recent wins with airline customers in Europe and the Americas, the Aeroitalia award reflects the increasing importance of component support solutions that help airlines maximize fleet reliability and aircraft availability. Delta recently reported the delivery of $1 billion in year-to-date MRO revenue, reflecting strong demand for the airline-tested expertise, operational experience and customer service that continue to differentiate Delta TechOps. Backed by the experience of maintaining one of the world's largest airline fleets, TechOps supports more than 150 customers across six continents. As North America's largest MRO provider, TechOps services more than 100,000 aircraft components annually through 25 in-house component shops and remains the only provider in the Americas certified to support the CFM LEAP, Pratt & Whitney GTF and Rolls-Royce Trent engine families.

stories.headline: European Aviation Network Traffic Drops 2.3% Week-on-Week Amid Weather Disruptions
stories.lead: European flight volumes fell to an average of 32,480 daily flights due to adverse weather and reduced capacity across major operators. Despite the weekly dip, overall network traffic remained 0.7% higher than the corresponding week in 2025.
stories.source_description: The network averaged 32,480 daily flights (including overflights), down 2.3% from Week 42 and 0.7% higher compared to the same week in 2025. Storms Austen and Boelo caused widespread flight disruptions across northern and western Europe between 23-25 October 2026. Among the 10 busiest carriers, capacity declined by an average of 1.3% week-on-week. Pegasus was the only carrier to record growth (+1%), while the KLM Group registered the largest decrease (-4%). Flight volumes across the 10 busiest States fell by an average of 2.5% with none recording growth. Greece saw the most significant decrease (-7%). Network arrival and departure punctuality were 73.5% and 69.4%, better than in the equivalent week of 2025. En-route ATFM delays decreased by 12% compared to the previous week, with a daily average of circa 54K delay minutes, and were 6% above 2025 levels. Total air traffic flow management (ATFM) delay was 2.4 min/flight (1.7 for en-route and 0.7 for airport). ATC capacity & staffing was the top delay cause (65% of all en-route ATFM delays), followed by weather (20%).

stories.lead: Boeing forecasts that the global commercial aircraft fleet will grow nearly 80% to over 50,000 airplanes by 2045. Airlines and cargo operators will require nearly 44,000 new aircraft over the next 20 years to support air travel and cargo expansion.

stories.lead: London Heathrow retained its title as the world's most connected airport for the third consecutive year in the OAG Megahubs 2025 ranking. Meanwhile, Istanbul Airport and Frankfurt registered substantial connectivity gains, while Tokyo Haneda experienced a decline.
stories.source_description: London Heathrow (LHR) retains its title as the world’s most connected airport for the third consecutive year , offering over 59,000 possible connections to 226 destinations* on the busiest day**. Frankfurt (FRA) has seen a significant shift in rankings, climbing from 10 th position last year to 4 th , driven by a 21% increase in potential connections year-on-year. Tokyo Haneda (HND) has dropped down in this year’s rankings from 3 rd in 2024 to 9 th in 2025, reflecting a 10% decline in connections. Atlanta Hartsfield-Jackson (ATL) – the world’s largest airport by seat capacity – re-enters the Top 10 this year rising from 11 th place last year to 8 th position in 2025. ATL has added eight (8) more destinations and seen a corresponding 14% increase in potential connections. stories.headline: Emirates Launches Redesigned Travel Store in Rome
stories.lead: Emirates has unveiled its refurbished Travel Store in Rome, making it the first in Italy to feature the airline's new global retail concept. Located in the EUR district, the venue is designed to support customer travel planning and sales.
stories.source_description: The first in Italy to feature its new global retail concept Rome, 28 October 2026 – Emirates today unveiled its redesigned Travel Store in Rome, the first in Italy to feature the reimagined retail concept the airline is rolling out across key markets in its global network. Located at 12 Via Chopin, in the EUR district, the store offers a contemporary and welcoming environment where customers can benefit from the expertise of Emirates’ travel consultants and the airline’s renowned hospitality as they plan their journeys. The opening ceremony was attended by Flavio Ghiringhelli, Emirates’ Vice President Regional Clusters for Southern and Central Europe , and Marco D’ilario, Emirates’ Manager for Italy , together with the airline’s commercial team, corporate clients, industry partners and Rome-based Emirates Skywards members. “The refurbishment of our Rome Travel Store represents a tangible investment in our customer relationships and in the Italian market. Rome is a key part of Emirates’ presence in Italy: an internationally connected city where the needs of businesses, professionals and individual travellers meet a diverse and dynamic tourism market. Bringing our new retail concept to Rome reinforces our commitment to this strategic market, enabling us to provide personalised support that caters to every traveller’s needs and requirements,” said Marco D’ilario, Emirates’ Manager for Italy . “Direct interaction allows us to better understand our customers and build lasting relationships by developing solutions tailored to their needs, from choosing the right itinerary to selecting services that make their journeys more comfortable and personal. This space brings Emirates’ hospitality closer to customers and businesses in the local community, strengthening relationships that grow over time, one journey at a time”. Opening this reimagined retail concept in Rome’s business and financial district compliments Emirates’ advanced digital presence by offering personalised travel support with a human touch for its customers in Italy. From itinerary planning to product selection and additional services, Emirates’ dedicated travel professionals will help customers tailor their travel arrangements to their individual needs. Customers with more complex requirements can further benefit from dedicated appointments with dedicated consultants. This service is particularly valuable for customers travelling in premium cabins, frequent flyers and small and medium-sized enterprises that manage their own business travel. Investing in Emirates’ Global Retail Experience The reimagined Rome Travel Store is part of Emirates’ global initiative to expand and refresh its retail presence, with stores that combine expert travel advice, the airline’s brand identity and a customer-centric approach to service. The airline has invested AED 174 million (USD$47.4 million) in this expansion plan and has already rolled out 10 Emirates World Stores and 13 travel retail outlets globally including Rome. Emirates Skywards members, the loyalty programme of Emirates and flydubai, will also enjoy bespoke support by visiting the store. Travel consultants can help members make the most of opportunities to earn and redeem Miles, understand the benefits associated with their membership tier, including Platinum, and discover the services available to further enhance their travel experience. The Emirates Travel Store in Rome is located at 12 Via Chopin, in the EUR district. It is open Monday to Friday, from 9 am to 5 pm. Emirates in Italy The refurbishment of the Rome Travel Store further strengthens Emirates’ presence in Italy, a strategic market served through four gateways: Rome Fiumicino, Milan Malpensa, Venice and Bologna . The airline currently operates 49 weekly flights between Italy and Dubai , connecting passengers via its Dubai hub to more than 140 destinations across its global network. Emirates also operates a non-stop, daily service between Milan Malpensa and New York JFK.

stories.headline: KLM Launches First Airbus A350-900 Passenger Flight to Toronto
stories.lead: KLM's first Airbus A350-900, named "De Nachtwacht," has completed its inaugural commercial flight from Amsterdam Schiphol to Toronto.
stories.source_description: KLM’s first Airbus A350-900 departed Schiphol for Toronto today. Flight KL0691 marks the aircraft’s first flight with passengers and eight metric tons of cargo on board. The aircraft is named De Nachtwacht (“The Night Watch”). Among the passengers were enthusiastic aviation fans who had booked tickets especially for the inaugural flight. Rien and Bob were among them. For the occasion, they had T-shirts printed with the text “1st commercial flight A350-900 AMS-YYZ.” This was the fifth time Rien had attended a first or last flight. He had previously been there for the final flights of the MD-11 and Fokker aircraft, and the first flights of the Dreamliner and the A321neo. Bob joined him for those occasions. “I was also at the first A321neo flight. It still smelled brand-new then, and I expect it will again this time. As a Platinum for Life member, I really wanted to experience this. It’s a special moment, and KLM can be proud of this important milestone. I hope I’ll get to experience just how much quieter this aircraft really is.” Father and son Ethan and Derrick also traveled all the way from New York to Amsterdam for the occasion. They landed at Schiphol this morning and, after Toronto, will continue on to New York. The arrival of the A350 marks an important step in KLM’s major fleet renewal program, which aims to make flying cleaner, quieter and more fuel-efficient. After Toronto, the aircraft will serve Montreal, Kilimanjaro, Dar es Salaam, Nairobi and Zanzibar. Photos: Arnoud Raeven

stories.headline: Emirates expands Premium Economy to Durban with deployment of A350
stories.lead: Emirates will introduce its A350 aircraft and Premium Economy cabin to Durban starting in March 2027, completing its premium rollout across South African gateways.
stories.source_description: · All three of Emirates’ gateways in South Africa are now served with the award-winning Premium Economy cabin · Since launching in Cape Town and Johannesburg in 2025, Premium Economy has maintained a healthy load factor for both in- and outbound passengers Durban, South Africa, 30 October 2026 – Emirates, the world’s largest international airline, is deploying the A350 to Durban from 1 March 2027 on its daily EK 775/776 service, expanding the roll out of Premium Economy to all South African gateways. Beyond introducing the airline’s newest cabin to Durban, the A350 brings the airline’s latest inflight experience to the KwaZulu-Natal province. Emirates first launched Premium Economy in both Cape Town and Johannesburg in September 2025 and, over the last 12 months, has seen consistently high demand for the airline’s newest cabin, driven equally by both leisure and corporate travellers. A significant percentage of travel in and out of Durban consists of visiting friends and family internationally, with passengers connecting via Dubai into key destinations such as Thailand, Indonesia, India, France and the UK. Now passengers will be able to enjoy their entire long-haul journey to all these destinations in Premium Economy. Afzal Parambil, Regional Manager for Southern Africa, Emirates , said: “We look forward to welcoming travellers from Durban onboard the A350 in the new year, where they can experience elevated onboard amenities and Emirates’ signature service that make this aircraft a passenger favourite. The deployment also reflects our broader commitment to South Africa, with all our gateways now offering the latest inflight experience. South Africa remains an anchor of our African network, with some of the busiest gateways globally, and we are committed to continually enhancing the travel experience for our customers by providing them with more choice, connectivity and comfort.” A closer look at the A350 As the newest aircraft type to join the Emirates’ fleet of all widebody aircraft, the A350 is equipped with the latest technology, enhanced entertainment options and all new cabin design focused on providing more space and comfort while travelling to elevate the in-flight experience. The highlight is Emirates’ award-winning Premium Economy cabin that has been likened to a Business Class experience on other airlines, with its soft, cream leather seats that offer generous legroom and recline, in-seat charging points, a wood-finished side cocktail table and a 13.3-inch personal entertainment screen. Laid out in 2-4-2 configuration, Premium Economy is the ideal upgrade for comfortable long-haul family travel or solo adventurers looking for extra space. Premium Economy passengers also enjoy a dedicated check-in counter and priority boarding at King Shaka International Airport, generous check-in baggage allowance of 35kg and a further 10kg of carry-on baggage. Business Class is configured in a 1-2-1 layout providing every passenger with direct aisle access and a spacious, private environment to work or relax in. The fully lie-flat seat is wrapped in soft cream leather and features a personal minibar and wireless charging for comfort and convenience. At the back of the cabin is a snack display area allowing passengers to help themselves to refreshments throughout the flight. Economy Class features an airy colour palette of sky blue, bronze and cream, complemented by lighter-toned wood finishings. The high, sweeping ceilings of the aircraft create a sense of space, while the ambient lighting helps passengers relax into the journey. Every screen on the aircraft features Emirates’ upgraded ice inflight entertainment system. With improved navigation, controls and search, it is easier than ever to explore over 6,500 channels of content including podcasts, movies, TV series, music, digital newspapers and much, much more. Passengers can also pair their Bluetooth headphones with the A350 to use their own device while tuned into ice. As always, customers can enjoy gourmet, regionally-inspired menus prepared by Emirates' chefs, accompanied by a carefully curated selection of premium beverages, including Journey’s End Weather Station Sauvignon Blanc 2025 , produced by the family-owned estate near Stellenbosch, South Africa in Economy and Vilafonté Series C 2016 , one of South Africa’s highly regarded fine wines, in First Class. For more information or to book tickets, visit emirates.com . Tickets can also be booked on Emirates App, Emirates Retail stores, Emirates contact centre, or via travel agents. Emirates continues to offer flexible booking policies and industry-first, comprehensive travel insurance, for added peace of mind while travelling.

stories.headline: Emirates Group Launches 10th Dubai Fitness Challenge for Employees
stories.lead: Emirates Group has commenced the 10th edition of the Dubai Fitness Challenge, with thousands of employees expected to participate in community events.
stories.source_description: Dubai, UAE, 30 October 2026 : Close to 24,000 Emirates Group employees are expected to participate in this year’s Dubai Fitness Challenge (DFC), reflecting the organisation’s longstanding commitment to the health and wellbeing of its workforce as it continues to champion initiatives that encourage its people to embrace active, healthy lifestyles. The Group’s efforts also support Dubai’s wider vision of becoming one of the world’s most active cities. The Emirates Group will participate in two of DFC’s flagship community events, Dubai Ride and Dubai Run. More than 3,200 employees from across the Group took part in Dubai Run in 2025. This year, the Group aims to exceed 4,000 registrations for Dubai Run on 22 November, with employees already signed up for Dubai Ride taking place on 1 November. Throughout the month, the Group’s more than 20 sports and hobby clubs are also actively participating in the Dubai Fitness Challenge with the Emirates Engineering Cricket Club joining the official DFC tournament, with fixtures beginning from 4 November. The Emirates Road Cycling Club will be joining the Dubai Ride, while the Emirates Paddling Club will participate in the fourth edition of the Dubai Stand Up Paddle (SUP) taking place on 7 and 8 November. The Emirates Group Basketball Club will also be competing in a tournament set to run from 4 November to 26 November. Marking 10 years of the Dubai Fitness Challenge, members of the Emirates Scuba Diving Club took the celebration underwater, with four employee divers entering The Lost Chambers Aquarium at Atlantis, The Palm to unveil a sign ‘ We’re celebrating 10 years of DFC, what’s your 30x30?’, a reminder that fitness can take any form. The Group has also organised a corporate fitness session at the Za’abeel Park Fitness Village, where close to 300 employees will train side by side with other colleagues from across the organisation. Complementing these activities, the Group’s wellbeing programme Sehaty will share practical fitness, nutrition and mental wellbeing tips with employees throughout the month. Sehaty runs year-round health awareness campaigns, supported by teams including Group Medical Services, Clinical Psychology and the Employee Assistance Programme, helping employees build healthier habits at work and at home. The Emirates Official Store also unveiled its latest EK FIT and EK TRAVEL collections, just in time for DFC, offering performance wear, accessories and loungewear in a palette of navy, almond, burgundy and olive. With prices starting from AED 55, the collection is available to shop at emirates.store and at Emirates Official Stores across Dubai. The Dubai Fitness Challenge runs from 31 October to 29 November 2026. This year, permanent employees who register and complete 30 minutes of physical activity or 10,000 steps every day for 30 days will also receive one Service-Related Concession ticket to anywhere on the Emirates network of close to 140 destinations, to further encourage employees to stay fit and adopt healthy activities.

stories.headline: Delta Introduces '48 Horas con Delta' Travel Content Series for Corporate Travelers
stories.lead: Delta Air Lines has launched a new travel video series featuring host Iván de Pineda, highlighting U.S. travel destinations for business passengers with extended stay opportunity.
stories.source_description: What do you do when work takes you somewhere new and you suddenly have a little extra time? That's the question behind 48 Horas con Delta , a new content series featuring Iván de Pineda, the Argentine television host and travel storyteller known for helping audiences discover destinations through history, culture and local perspective. The series is rooted in a familiar travel reality: a business trip that leaves room to explore. An extra day before heading home. A free afternoon between meetings. A destination you've visited before, but never really experienced. At the beginning of every episode, De Pineda introduces the journey with the same thought: "Si viajas por trabajo y tenés unos días extras para conocer una ciudad, estos son los imperdibles." Across eight U.S. destinations, he shares the places, neighborhoods and experiences that help travelers make the most of a short stay. Rather than offering a traditional checklist of attractions, 48 Horas con Delta focuses on what gives each city its character. In Atlanta, De Pineda explores the city's civil rights legacy, local neighborhoods and cultural landmarks. 48 Horas con Delta en Atlanta - con Iván de Pineda Remote video URL In Boston, he traces the city's identity through its history, public spaces and world-renowned academic institutions. Remote video URL In Miami, he highlights the communities, creativity and cultural influences that continue to shape one of the country's most dynamic destinations. Remote video URL Other episodes take viewers to New York , San Francisco , Seattle, Dallas and Kansas City , where the focus remains the same: helping travelers connect with a place beyond its most recognizable landmarks. In New York, that means discovering neighborhoods like the West Village and experiencing the city from the High Line and the Hudson waterfront. In San Francisco, it means understanding the history behind the city's cable cars, waterfront and hills. In Seattle, it means exploring Pike Place Market, Capitol Hill and the city's maritime heritage. In Dallas and Kansas City, it means experiencing the local culture, food and traditions that define each community. For De Pineda, whose career has been shaped by curiosity and exploration, the concept is simple: when travel creates an unexpected opportunity to discover somewhere new, even a few hours can be enough to see a destination differently. And sometimes, all it takes is 48 hours.

stories.headline: Emirates to Upgrade All Vietnam Routes to Airbus A350 Aircraft by 1 December
stories.lead: Emirates is expanding its Vietnam network operations by introducing additional frequencies and transitioning all daily flights to Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City to Airbus A350 aircraft.
stories.source_description: Airline to debut its A350 in Hanoi on 1 December Ho Chi Minh City will receive twice-daily A350 services from 1 November HANOI, Vietnam, 28 October 2026— Emirates is strengthening its offering in Vietnam with additional frequencies, expanded Airbus A350 operations and the introduction of Premium Economy in Hanoi . The airline will introduce a second daily A350 service between Dubai and Ho Chi Minh City on flights EK364/365 from 1 November. From 1 December, Emirates will also deploy its Airbus A350 on the two daily services between Dubai and Hanoi, flights EK394/395 and EK388/389. With these enhancements, all four daily flights connecting Dubai with Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City will be operated by Emirates’ newest aircraft type by 1 December, offering customers a consistent onboard experience featuring the airline’s award-winning Premium Economy cabin and latest products. Wahid Albalooshi, Country Manager of Emirates Vietnam said: “Vietnam continues to be an important market for Emirates, and these enhancements build on the airline’s ongoing investments here. Just last year, we launched operations to Da Nang, expanding our footprint in Vietnam across three major gateways. By deploying our best products in this market, we will ensure that travellers will receive a more consistent travel experience not only between Vietnam and Dubai, but also to other popular cities served by the Emirates Airbus A350.” The Emirates’ Airbus A350 experience The A350, the newest aircraft type to join Emirates’ all-widebody fleet, carries 298 passengers across three spacious cabins: Business, Premium Economy and Economy. Bright and airy interior cabins have been thoughtfully designed to provide more space and comfort, whilst cutting-edge technology and enhanced entertainment options elevate every journey. Emirates’ Premium Economy cabin offers elevated comfort, comparable to a Business Class experience on many airlines. Spacious with leather reclining seats that feature a generous pitch, adjustable headrests and more legroom. Customers also enjoy in-seat charging points, a wood-finished side cocktail table, a 13.3-inch TV screen, a generously sized pillow and blanket, complimentary amenity kits on select flights, and the globally exclusive Chandon Vintage Brut 2017 sparkling wine. Business Class is configured in a 1-2-1 layout, giving every passenger direct aisle access and a spacious, private setting for both work or relaxation. Each fully lie-flat seat is upholstered in soft cream leather and includes a personal minibar and wireless charging. At the back of the cabin is a snack display area allowing passengers to help themselves to refreshments throughout the flight. Economy Class features an all new, airy colour palette of sky blue, bronze and cream, complemented by lighter-toned wood finishes. Each seat includes the airline’s upgraded ice inflight entertainment system on a 13.3-inch, 4K adjustable touchscreen, while generous seat pitch and leather headrests provide added support, comfort and extra legroom. With the introduction of Premium Economy in Hanoi and expanded A350 operations in Ho Chi Minh City, Emirates is further enhancing its product offering for travellers across Vietnam’s two largest aviation gateways. Tickets can be booked now on emirates.com, the Emirates App, or via both online and offline travel agents. Vietnamese travellers may be eligible for a UAE visa on arrival if they hold a valid residence permit issued by the US, UK, an EU member state, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Japan or South Korea.
